document.title: Developments in Afghanistan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Unknown] As the Taliban emerge as a major player, a source (name excised) is troubled by Pakistan's deep involvement in Afghan politics and its role in the Taliban's recent successes. He says the ISI is deeply involved in the Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat, and that Pakistan's agenda will sabotage UN peace efforts led by Mahmoud Mestiri.

events.description: Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat, allegedly with deep ISI involvement.
Memo reporting weekend concerns on Afghan network about Pakistani involvement in southern and western Afghanistan.
Alleged Rabbani–ISI deal permitting ISI move into southern and western Afghanistan provided it does not challenge Ismail Khan in Herat.
Alleged Pakistan Air Force preparation of Kandahar airport to support larger Taliban operations in Helmand and Farah.
Taliban take over Kandahar and Qalat, allegedly with ISI involvement.
Reported Rabbani-ISI deal permitting an ISI move into south and west Afghanistan without challenging Ismail Khan in Herat.
Alleged Pakistan Air Force preparation of Kandahar airport to support larger operations in Helmand and Farah.

key_claims: ISI is alleged to be deeply involved in the Taliban takeover of Kandahar and Qalat.
Pakistan may be seeking to pacify Afghanistan to open a Central Asia–Karachi trade route via the Herat–Kandahar–Chaman road.
An alleged Rabbani–ISI deal accepts ISI moves into the south and west as long as Ismail Khan's Herat is not challenged.
A widening gulf between ISI and Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, caused by the Kabul stalemate, is being exploited by Rabbani.
Pakistan Air Force is alleged to be readying Kandahar airport to support larger Taliban operations in Helmand and Farah.
Former Khalqis are alleged to serve as enforcers for the Taliban in Kandahar.
The author warns that Pakistani intervention will generate resistance in the south and long-term instability, and may undermine the UN (Mestiri) plan.
